name: v0.3.0
body:
### Breaking

- `bay release` goes only to the remote's default branch: a branch whose upstream (or, with none, its own name) is another branch is refused by name, where it was released to that branch, so every release is on one line.
- `bay --workspace release` refuses a train whose members do not each say they are the family's, `"policy": "family"` in their `ci/preflight.json`, naming each one without it, or with another policy, before anything moves. bay never writes the key.
- Commit pins of one package that diverge, none containing the others, are refused, each named with who pins it: pin a commit that contains them all. The highest version their manifests said was selected, and it silently lacked the other branch's commits. A package pinned at a commit and by an archive is refused too, as history cannot place an archive.

### Added

- `bay release` gates a package on GitHub before its tag, where its `ci.yml` dispatches a release tier: the release commit is pushed to `release/vX.Y.Z`, the tier dispatched on it with the person's own login (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, else `gh auth token`; bay stores no token) and waited on, each job said as it ends, one hosted run at a time on the machine. Green, main and the tag go in one atomic push that deletes the candidate. Red, the candidate is deleted, the failing jobs and the run named and the branch put back, and nothing is tagged. A gated commit whose push failed keeps its run for the next `bay release`.
- `bay audit releases` checks each release tag of the package's GitHub repository, from the first release gated there on: an annotated tag whose `Gated-by` run was a green release tier on its commit and candidate branch, and a GitHub Release whose notes name that run. Each tag that falls short is named with what it lacks, and the command fails; the tags before are named once, as history. It reads git and GitHub only, with the person's login where there is one.
- `bay pin <dependency> <version>` moves the package onto a dependency's release as a workspace's train moves a member: pinned at the tag and tidied, "Pins x 1.2.0." under `### Changed`, committed, gated and pushed. It is released when `[Unreleased]` held entries before; a re-pin alone is pushed with no tag, its entry waiting for the next release. `--dry-run` says which.
- `bay man` writes bay's manual pages (ensign's `writeManPage`): `bay man add` the page of `bay add`, for `man -l -`, and `bay man --directory DIR` every page, as `bay.1`, `bay-add.1` and the rest, for a man path. Each carries the version and the day its CHANGELOG heading gives it.
- `bay release` takes an archive that is no Zig package (no `build.zig.zon`: its hash is `N-V-…`, a tree-sitter grammar, a body of queries) pinned at its exact commit, which with its hash fixes it as a tag would; a Zig package is still released at a version tag, and a branch or any ref that moves is refused for both, the refusal naming which case it is. Every grammar archive ztreesitter pins was refused as "no version tag of its repository", though none has versions to tag.
- A NuGet pin can hold the package's author signature to a root: `bay add --nuget --nuget-root <url> --nuget-root-sha256 <hex>` pins `.publisher = .{ .nuget = .{ .root, .root_sha256 } }`. Wherever bay downloads the package it checks the signature with cloak's `cloak-nuget-check` (the chain to that root, at the time the signature's timestamp proves, and the package hash the signature names), built once from the cloak bay pins with the Zig it manages and kept by cloak's hash. The root certificate is fetched from its URL when pinning and kept by its SHA-256. `bay outdated` lists the root beside the pin. A plain `.nuget` stays nuget.org's catalog hash.
- `bay release` publishes the tag's GitHub Release on a remote at github.com, after the push. Its notes are the version's CHANGELOG section. Where the build has a `dist` step, it also carries the programs that step installs into `dist`, built from the release commit, and their `SHA256SUMS`. `GITHUB_TOKEN` authorizes it, and `GITHUB_API_URL` names another server, as GitHub's runners set it. A release pushed without a token, or one that stopped part way, is finished by the next `bay release` at the tag: GitHub keeps the release once made, and only the files it does not yet hold are uploaded. `--dry-run` names the release it would publish.
- OpenPGP detached signatures are verified as RFC 9580 verifies a version 4 signature over a binary document, on std alone: RSA (PKCS #1 v1.5) or Ed25519 over SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, by a key from a file, binary or armored, every block of a keyring file read. The file is the only trust: no keyring, web of trust or key server is consulted. SHA-1, text signatures and a hashed critical subpacket bay does not know are refused. MSYS2 signs its packages so (RSA over SHA-512); its signature over `mingw-w64-clang-x86_64-vulkan-validation-layers-1.4.363.0-1` verifies with MSYS2's keyring.
- A prebuilt archive is unpacked by bay itself, through hold's tar and zip readers and warp's gzip and zstd decoders, only once it is authenticated: its size and SHA-256 those its pin holds, then its publisher's signature, before a byte of it is read as an archive, so its integrity rests on those and not on the archive's own checksums. Three formats, told by their first bytes: a tar in gzip, a tar in zstd (a window above 128 MiB refused from the frame's header) and a zip of stored or deflated entries, as a NuGet package is. xz and bzip2 are refused by name, as is an encrypted zip entry or one compressed otherwise, naming it; a zip's directory is checked against the archive's bounds before any entry is read, and an entry whose bytes are not its declared size or whose CRC-32 is not theirs is refused. The archive is read twice, once to check every entry and write nothing, once to write it: a name that is absolute, climbs out with `..` or that some system cannot hold (a backslash, `:`, a control byte, a Windows device name, a trailing dot or space), two names one where case folds, a hard link or a device, a link out of the tree, and a tree larger than the pin allows are each refused, naming the entry. The tree is the one Zig's fetch makes: a single top directory taken away, empty directories dropped, links written last, programs marked by their first bytes. git's checkout writes its tree through the same code.
- Prebuilt pins: a library or tool that ships only built, in an archive Zig's fetch does not take, is pinned behind a `bay+https://` URL. `bay add --name <name>` pins it once its publisher vouches for it: a minisign key (`--minisign`, the signature at the URL plus `.minisig`, its trusted comment naming the file), an OpenPGP key file the package ships (`--openpgp`, at the URL plus `.sig`), nuget.org's catalog for a package on api.nuget.org (`--nuget`, its SHA-512 read from the index at `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json`; another feed is refused by name), or none (`--no-publisher`). The pin records the archive's `.sha256` and `.size`, its `.publisher`, its `.license` (the tree's one licence file, else `--license <path>`), and the hash Zig gives its tree. Wherever bay downloads it (`bay add`, `bay update`, a machine without it), the archive is downloaded no further than its size, checked against its digest and its publisher before it is unpacked, unpacked within the size the hash records, and handed to Zig's cache by `zig fetch`, whose hash must be the pin's; bay keeps it in its data directory by its digest, one download at a time, so a cleared cache fills again offline. A build brings the prebuilts it takes before it runs, a lazy one only when its configuration asks for it; `bay fetch` and `bay vendor` bring every one. Plain http is refused but to this machine's loopback address by number. `bay update <name> <bay+https://…>` moves one to another URL with the same checks; `bay outdated` does not list prebuilts, as no version protocol is common to their sources, and says so; `bay licenses` lists each by its pin's name with what its licence file states, or that bay does not read it. A licence or key file a dependency's pin names must be inside its tree or package. A `bay+` pin needs bay: `zig build` takes one once `bay fetch` has put it in Zig's cache.
- `bay licenses` knows Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception by its wording, as libc++ ships it; it said Apache-2.0.
- An upstream with no `build.zig.zon` (a C library's repository, a set of headers), which Zig names by its hash alone, is known by the key that pins it and by its URL: the repository, and the tag a git URL's `?ref=` names, or a GitHub `archive/refs/tags/<tag>` archive or `releases/download/<tag>/` asset. `bay outdated` compares that tag with the repository's tags named the same way (`v1.15`, `VER-2-13-3`; a pre-release never), and `bay licenses` and `bay tree` print the key and the tag. `bay audit` matches the tag against the advisories of the repository the URL comes from. Before, `outdated` passed such a package over, `licenses` listed it as `N-V-… 0.0.0`, and `audit` said only "not read for N-V-…". A series of patches over it in `patches/<key>`, which retrofit applies in the package's build, is counted beside its tag (`+ 2 patches`).

### Changed

- bay's own development holds it to the family's policy: `"policy": "family"` in ci/preflight.json, beside the hardened profile ci/workflow.json already declares, so its release tier runs the profile on shakedown's quarantine and refuses a rule set below its default.
- A release's tag is annotated, its message the version and, where GitHub's release tier passed it, a `Gated-by:` line with the run's page, which the GitHub Release's notes link too. It was a lightweight tag.
- `bay release` publishes the GitHub Release with `gh`'s login where `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not set.
- `bay release` takes a development pin at an exact commit (a git pin whose fragment is a full commit, with or without the ref it was fetched from) until preflight 0.19.0 and shakedown 0.7.0 are released, read from the repositories of the package's own pins on them, and names each such pin in its output. A runtime pin is still held to a version tag, and a branch or a ref that moves is refused for both. It refused every development pin at no release.
- The family move: aegis f52eabe, the one aegis the family moves to, with the dependencies on it moved (hold d5a0f2f, warp 0e8a04d, airlock 3ef2f54, ensign 1e6ff3c), and preflight ci-standard 158c176 and shakedown c29751d in the development build; ci.yml regenerated. No glint-ignore is left in bay: a store takes the project's cloak from the manifest its caller read, where it read the manifest a second time and passed over a failure; text that is no semantic version is `remote.semantic`'s null; the cloak tool's scratch directories are removed through `cleared`, which says one it cannot remove and returns that note's failure; a kept NuGet root that cannot be read is said before it is downloaded again; a gate's lines after one the terminal or its log refused are read and dropped, so the gate runs to its end, the refusal still ending the release.
- Pins hold 47bf34e and warp 79a4611 (new: the archive readers; hold's zip and tar readers carry fuzzed crafted-input properties of their own), airlock 0f9e915 (hold's), preflight ci-standard f991816 and shakedown 327bc61 in the development build; ci.yml regenerated (`bay generate`).
- Pins aegis c8982a8, still 0.2.4: six additive commits after 3c0b13e (the role declarations a linter reads, `lint_rules`), the aegis the development build's preflight selects. Nothing bay calls changed.
- The README states bay's stability policy (0.x, tracking Zig 0.17.x; a breaking change to its commands or manifest keys only in a minor release, with its CHANGELOG entry; a patch release never breaks), where it said work was in progress.
- The contracts left on `std.debug.assert` (a re-pin's list, a tidy's manifest, a release's change) are `aegis.assert.invariant`: they hold in every build.
- Pins aegis breaking-0.3 (3c0b13e), with airlock, ensign and shakedown at their commits on it, where `Owned.lend()` is gone: a package directory or a machine's stdin is lent by value, `borrow().*`, and `bay each` waits on its board's guard (`guard.waitUncancelable(&changed, io, .none)`); airlock (reflink-lock) and shakedown on it.
- A package's commit pins are ordered by its git history, not by the versions their manifests say: between releases many commits carry one version. bay selects the commit every other pinned commit is an ancestor of, a release counting as the commit its tag names, as Go orders pseudo-versions by their commits. A release and a commit descending from its tag select the commit; commits on one line select the newest. Such graphs were refused as "two contents" of one version, or as "a different line" when a fix's commit still said the version before the release it was merged into. A pin is a release when it is a git pin whose `?ref=` is the tag of the version its manifest says, or a pin of no commit (an archive); a graph of releases alone is selected by version as before and fetches nothing more. To order commits, bay keeps each package's history in its data directory (`history/<name>-<fingerprint>.git`): commit objects alone (`--filter=tree:0`), each commit fetched once from its own pin's repository. `bay release` still refuses a pin at no release.
- `bay tidy --dry-run` says what tidy would pin and which build's `generate` step it would then run, and writes and runs nothing. A train's dry run runs it in each member, then lists the car's steps (the re-pin, the release commit, the gate and where, the push): the first family train went red at a `generate` step its dry run never looked at.
- One train per workspace and one gate per directory on a machine: each holds a lock in bay's data directory, and a second refuses by name, saying since when the first holds it. Two trains once gated one copy at once, and the second's build failed on a file the first was writing.
- `bay release` refuses a manifest whose git pins name no release: each `?ref=` must be a version tag on its repository at the commit the pin holds, dependencies, development dependencies and overrides alike, each one named. A forge's archive pin (`/owner/repo/archive/<revision>` on GitHub, Codeberg, Forgejo or Gitea, GitHub's `tarball` and `zipball`, api.github.com and codeload, GitLab's `/-/archive/` under any depth of groups, Bitbucket's `/get/`) must name a version tag or the commit one names: an archive of a commit no tag names was taken as a release. A URL on a known forge (github.com, api.github.com, codeload.github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org, codeberg.org, whatever the host's case) that bay cannot read as one of those is refused, as is one there with an empty path segment, a query or not https: it passed on its hash. A URL on any other host names no repository bay can read, and its hash fixes what its host published. Released tags of the family carried development pins on branches (`?ref=aegis-0.2`, `?ref=enforcement`): fixed by their commits, but at code no tag fixes.
- A commit `bay release` gated green and has not pushed is recorded in bay's data directory (`gated/<repository>/<tag>`), where it was a ref, `refs/bay/gated/<tag>`: a ref travels with a fetch, a bundle or a mirror clone, and one made by hand was taken as a gate passed. Only this machine's gate writes the record now.
- `bay release` fetches every remote pin, as Zig records it, and refuses one whose `.hash` is not what its URL holds, naming both: Zig takes a package its cache holds by the hash alone, so a hash of other content built here and passed.
- `bay release` and `bay --workspace release`, and a machine's side of either, build with the Zig each package's manifest names and ignore a `ZIG` the shell set: a stand-in for Zig that passed every build called the gate green.
- The gate `bay release` runs on this machine is given no `PREFLIGHT_PORTABLE`, so it runs the jobs that say the same on any machine (the source checks), as the machine that releases must: an `elsewhere` it inherited from the shell left them to no machine, and the gate came out green with them unproven. Only a machine beside it is told `elsewhere`.
- `bay tidy`, and with it every command that tidies and a train's re-pin, gives each other manifest under the package (a sample, a fixture, a conformance build) the package's own `.url` and `.hash` for each package both pin remotely, and names each move. preflight's lint asks for exactly this, and nothing wrote it: preflight's `sample/bay` kept developing with shakedown 0.4.17 when preflight moved on, so bay refused the sample in preflight 0.18.2's gate ("pinned below the selection"). A package only the nested manifest pins, or takes by path, stays as it is, and hidden directories, `zig-out` and `zig-pkg` are not read. `--locked` refuses a nested manifest that would change.
- `bay release` refuses a package inside a workspace with other members (a `bay.work` in its directory or one above), naming the file and the members. Their working trees would stand in for what the package pins, so the gate would pass on code no release holds: aegis 0.2.2's gate once ran under a stray `bay.work`, developed with unreleased glint and preflight. `bay --workspace release` still releases the members, each in the workspace it was made for.
- `bay release` on a branch with no upstream pushes it to its own name on the remote, as `git push -u` would, and makes that its upstream: the remote git pushes to by default (`remote.pushDefault`), or the one remote there is. It refused the branch before, asking for `git push -u` first. With more than one remote and none the default, it still refuses, naming that. A dry run says the branch would take the upstream.
- Pins aegis 0.4.0, ensign 0.4.0, airlock 0.7.0, hold 0.2.0 and warp 0.5.0.
- `bay` with no command asks the terminal for its width with a `try`: ensign 0.4.0's `terminalWidth` returns `Canceled` for a cancel that lands while asking, which bay now passes on instead of failing to build.

### Fixed

- A `bay.work` holds only its members. A package below a workspace's file that the workspace lists neither by directory nor as a checkout of a member (a scratch clone of something else) took the members as main modules all the same: a fresh blackbox clone under a workspace developing a WIP glint was refused, its aegis "diverging" through that glint's pins. It now builds with its own pins.
- A dependency's development pins are not read. Selection read every pin of every revision it reached and counted what they reached among a package's candidates, so a commit only a dependency's `.dev_dependencies` reach, in no build of it or of anything depending on it, could make a package's pins "diverge". A main module's development pins are read as before.
- A refusal that names who pins a revision also prints the chain of pins from the root that reaches it, each revision by name and version and a directory one by its path (`reached by app 0.1.0 (at …) > uplink 0.1.0`).
- No run of bay fails without a sentence. A program bay runs and waits for (Zig for `bay build`, `bay dev` and `bay <step>`, `zig init`, an install's build, a machine's `bay gate`) that was ended by a signal, or stopped, ended the run with code 1 and nothing said; bay now names how it ended (`zig was ended by signal 9 (KILL) before it exited`). A build listing that does not configure and wrote nothing is named too, with its exit code.
- A crafted archive no longer stops bay. A zip whose central directory record's name, extra and comment lengths passed 64 KiB together stopped it in std's zip reader (an integer overflow; undefined in a ReleaseFast build), and std's tar, gzip, zstd and xz readers were reached by archive bytes too. Every archive bay reads now goes through hold's readers and warp's decoders, whose lengths are checked: a prebuilt's, Zig's toolchain archive (its tar.xz, or its zip on Windows), and a package Zig keeps in its cache (`p/<hash>.tar.gz`). The last two are written by hold's extraction, names and links kept inside the tree.
- `bay outdated` names each package it cannot check and why ("not checked: blob (its URL names no tag)"). Its "every package is at its newest release" line then says "every package checked". It said every package was newest while it had passed over the packages with no manifest, and the packages pinned by an archive URL.
- `bay audit` reads the advisories of a package pinned by a GitHub archive URL from the repository the archive comes from. It refused the URL's `/archive/…` path, so the package was "not read".
- A pin bay rewrites in place (`bay add` of a name already there, `bay update`, `bay tidy`, a train's re-pin) no longer leaves a blank line after it in the manifest.
- `bay install` takes a repository's URL as `bay add` does: `https://github.com/owner/repo`, as a browser shows it, is the git repository there, and a git URL that names no ref installs the newest release. It handed the page's URL to Zig's fetch, which refused the HTML, and installed a bare git URL from the default branch's head. Both commands now find the source one way, and a `git+ssh` or `git+file` URL with no ref takes the newest release too, where `bay add` pinned its default branch.
- A cancel stops bay where it lands: finding the package or the one around it, `bay init` and `bay new` asking whether a manifest is there, a machine's gate asking whether its clone is there, `bay add` asking whether the source is a directory, and `bay licenses` reading a package's directory each took a cancel for an answer (no manifest, no clone, a name to fetch, no license) and went on: `bay init` ran `zig init`, a machine's gate ran `git init`. A ref that cannot be followed for want of memory is no longer read as a pin at a bare commit.

Gated by the release tier on GitHub: https://github.com/pedronaugusto/bay/actions/runs/45044490966
